pages.title: Exoplanetology
pages.text: $(thing)Exoplanetology$()$(br2)Most stars have planets. Watch a star's light dip as one crosses in front of it, and the dip gives its size; its spectrum through the planet's air gives what it is made of. Unlocks transit photometry and the assay of exoplanet cores.

$(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Spectroscopy.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Star Field Plate, 2 Stellar Spectrum Plate.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A planet of radius r crosses in front of its star, whose radius is R, and blocks part of its light. Write the fraction δ of the starlight that is lost, as a percentage.
